o1.biggest_strength: It builds a tiered COD-confirmation flow with calls and a 48-hour cancel rule aimed squarely at the Tier 3 band causing ~half the RTO cost, and prices each discount against the expected refusal loss it removes (₹70/₹41/₹27).
o1.biggest_mistake: Calls go to all ~260 Tier 3 COD orders a day through the same 4 agents who carry chats, which likely breaks the team and the 15-minute reply target; the capacity math isn't checked.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the agent-minutes math proving the Tier 3 call volume fits the 4-person team, or cap calls to the highest-risk slice, and fix the second template category so no marketing content sits in Utility.

o2.biggest_strength: Cleanest, most paste-ready set of templates with correct categories throughout, and a sharp operational fix: move one agent to a 2pm–midnight shift so the 31% after-hours wave gets a real person.
o2.biggest_mistake: It targets Tier 2 and Tier 3 with the same 48-hour hold-and-cancel rule and ships metros blindly, so it doesn't size the flow to the pincode risk the data points to, and its prepaid nudge gives away margin-free ease but no reason to switch.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Differentiate the confirmation and prepaid nudge by pincode risk with the RTO money worked out per band, and put the prepaid nudge incentive in a Marketing template so the switch actually happens.

reason: Output 1 wins on the owner's core question: it attacks the Tier 3 RTO money directly with a tiered flow, priced discounts and a holdout, while Output 2 is cleaner to submit but treats all COD orders alike. Both are strong; Output 1 is the one I'd pay more for because it moves the ₹11 lakh number.
